findings.title: Admission implementation executes before the accepted qualification hash check
findings.impact: The entry imports cpu_ledger_admission and calls input_pins before comparing its bytes with q.implementation_sha256. An altered or foreign already-imported admission module can therefore execute before the qualification implementation mismatch is rejected. This breaks the intended gate ordering even though later rejection prevents the normal analyze_pair call.
findings.bounded_probe: With an otherwise valid fake qualification expecting a different admission hash, an injected admission.input_pins spy executed before ValueError(actual CPU qualification implementation changed). No science modules were imported or files changed.
findings.fix: Validate every q implementation SHA against canonical helper/admission files before importing or calling any of them; also validate the imported admission module canonical path/identity if imports may be cached. Add a regression proving an admission callable is not reached on hash mismatch.

findings.title: CPU slot is scoped to a block instead of the required process lifetime, and scientific imports precede slot acquisition
findings.impact: cpu_slot explicitly unlocks and closes its stream on context exit, including main return while the interpreter is still alive. A new job can therefore acquire the same slot before true process exit, contrary to PLAN.md:3. The slot is also acquired after scientific imports, so a process can load torch/pandas/scientific modules before discovering that both CPU slots are occupied. Current legacy admission detection is conservative and working for the observed absolute command tokens.
findings.bounded_probe: Using a temporary fake root and no legacy processes, a second file descriptor was blocked inside cpu_slot, but acquired the lock immediately after scope exit while the same process remained alive. No real slot file or live process was touched.
findings.fix: Reserve the actual slot before scientific imports, then use a process-lifetime launch/lock mechanism or retain the kernel lock descriptor until OS process exit. Preserve both legacy reservations until true process exit. Add a subprocess regression proving the lock remains held after the with body and is released only after that process exits.
